script.1:
1. 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
M: Hello, visitors to Cryston Beach. This is an announcement from the management office. As you know, this beach is famous for its beautiful black stones.
Unfortunately, there were some cases where visitors damaged the beach by taking stones. To protect the beach, you must not take any stones from the beach. This is actually the law, so if you take any stones, you may have to pay a penalty of 1,000 dollars. Once again, do not take the stones from the beach. This will help protect its natural beauty and ecosystem. Please enjoy your time at Cryston Beach. Thank you.
script.2:
2. 대화를 듣고, 여자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
W: Mike, you look exhausted. Is everything okay?
M: Yes, Mom. I just feel tired because I have lots of social events these days.
W: Yeah, you’ve seemed busy meeting people.
M: It’s usually fun hanging out with others, but lately I feel mentally tired.
W: You know, having some time alone can recharge your energy.
M: Really? How does that help me regain energy?
W: Well, when meeting people, you use lots of energy. You have to listen carefully to what others say.
M: And it takes my full attention to respond to them.
W: Exactly. That’s why being a conversation partner takes so much energy.
M: It explains why my energy level is low these days.
W: Right. So, spending some time by yourself can refill your energy.
M: Okay. I’ll try that. Thanks, Mom.
script.3:
3. 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
W: Hello, viewers. I’m your life coach, Jinny Brown. Have you ever tried to accomplish a goal but failed? If so, reading your goals aloud before going to bed can help you to achieve them. When you do this before sleeping, your brain receives a signal that your goals are very important. This prepares your brain to focus on opportunities related to your goals the next day. Simply speaking, by reading your goals aloud before sleeping, your brain will search for ways to achieve them when you wake up. So, if you want your goals to become reality, it’s helpful to read your goals out loud before going to bed.
How about giving it a try tonight?
script.4:
4. 대화를 듣고, 그림에서 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
M: Lucy, I heard you stayed at your grandparents’ farm during the summer vacation.
How was it?
W: It was great. [Pause] Here, look at this picture.
M: Wow, it looks peaceful. There is a table between two chairs.
W: Yeah. We ate breakfast there often. It was a perfect place to eat.
M: You’re so lucky. I like the heart-patterned tablecloth.
W: My grandmother made it herself. Do you see the dog under the parasol? He’s my grandparents’ dog, Simba.
M: He’s very cute.
W: Yes, he is. You see the swing hanging from the tree, don’t you? I sat there to enjoy the view.
M: It must’ve been wonderful. Look! There are three sheep.
W: I even got to feed them. It was fun.
M: Sounds like you had the best summer.
script.5:
5. 대화를 듣고, 남자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
W: Hi, Mr. Smith. Our school library’s Book Cover Design Day is tomorrow.
Our students are excited about it.
M: Yes, they are, Ms. Thompson. Let’s make sure we’re ready for it.
W: Sure. I already prepared handouts for the participants.
M: Good. And yesterday, I printed the list of participating students.
W: Great. You ordered the gift badges for them, right?
M: I did, and they arrived this morning. I’m sure the students will love them.
W: Wonderful. Did you check if the scanner is working? The students will need to scan their book cover designs.
M: No, I didn’t. I’ll check it this afternoon.
W: Perfect. I’ll move the books and crayons to the library lobby while you’re doing that.
M: Thank you.
script.6:
6. 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
M: Welcome to the Cherrymarsh Bakery Fair. How may I help you?
W: Hi, I’d like to buy admission tickets.
M: Sure. Admission tickets are 15 dollars per adult and 10 dollars per child. How many tickets would you like?
W: I need two adult tickets and one child ticket.
M: All right. Would you be interested in a baking class as well? You’ll learn how to bake cookies.
W: Oh, my daughter will love it. How much is it?
M: It’s 10 dollars per person.
W: Then, one baking class ticket for my daughter, please.
M: Okay. So, that’s two adult admission tickets, one child admission ticket, and one baking class ticket, right?
W: That’s correct. Can I use this discount coupon?
M: Let me check. [Pause] Yes, you’ll get a 10 percent discount on the total purchase.
W: Great. Here’s my credit card.
script.7:
7. 대화를 듣고, 여자가 필라테스 수업을 그만둔 이유를 고르시오.
M: Hey, Grace. How are your Pilates lessons going?
W: Hi, Andy. Actually, I quit going to my Pilates lessons.
M: Why did you quit? You liked the class because it was not expensive.
W: Yeah. In fact, the lessons were the cheapest in town.
M: Then, was it because there were too many people in a lesson?
W: No, that wasn’t the problem. I usually did one-on-one sessions.
M: I see. Did you have an issue with the equipment?
W: No, I liked the equipment. It was all brand new.
M: Then, what was the problem?
W: Well, my instructor was often late for lessons.
M: Oh, no. You must’ve been disappointed. Now, what’s your plan?
W: I guess I’ll find another place.
M: I’m sure you will.
script.8:
8. 대화를 듣고, UXZ Time Capsule Event에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
W: Hi, Liam. Did you hear that our university is holding the UXZ Time Capsule Event?
M: A time capsule event? What’s the purpose?
W: It’s to celebrate our university’s 100th anniversary. They’re collecting meaningful items about campus life.
M: That’s interesting! Who can participate?
W: All professors and students can join in.
M: Good. Then, I’ll bring the medal I won at the English speech contest. Where can we submit our items?
W: We should take them to the student council office. I think I’ll bring my club T-shirt.
M: Nice idea. Do you know when we should submit our items?
W: They’re collecting items from this Wednesday until next Friday.
M: Great. Let’s take our items together this week.
script.9:
9. Senior Dinner Cruise에 관한 다음 내용을 듣고, 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
M: Hello, listeners. Are you looking for a perfect way to enjoy a memorable dinner on the water? I’m happy to tell you about the Senior Dinner Cruise.
This cruise is for those who are 55 years old or older. The cruise will run every day from October 1st until November 30th. This unforgettable dinner cruise includes a seafood buffet and a traditional dance performance. But due to our recent regulation changes, I’m afraid you cannot take your pets on the cruise. The price is 100 dollars, but if you book a group of at least four people, you’ll receive a 20 percent discount. And please remember that every passenger needs to bring their ID card. Don’t miss this opportunity to enjoy a relaxing dinner cruise for seniors. Thank you.
script.10:
10. 다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 예약할 우주 박물관 프로그램을 고르시오.
W: Honey, what are you looking at on your computer?
M: I’m looking at the Space Museum programs for our son, David. He’s interested in space these days. Can you help me choose one?
W: Sure, let me see. David is 11 years old, so this program for kids under 10 is not for him.
M: Right. As for the activities, we should not choose ‘Star Watching’ because he went to a star-watching event at school.
W: Good point. What about the program duration?
M: Hmm. I think this 70-minute program is too long for him. He can’t stay focused that long.
W: You’re right. Then, we have two options left. Should we go with the one that includes a 4D space movie?
M: Yeah. David would love it. He’s never watched one before.
W: True. Then, let’s book that program.
M: Sounds good.

15. 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Chris가 Judy에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
[3점] W: Chris and Judy are father and daughter. Judy likes posting pictures of herself on her social media account. Chris often sees her pictures when he’s on social media. One day, he notices her pictures are available for anyone to see. Chris starts to worry because he remembers reading a recent news article about the dangers of AI technology. The article said AI can easily generate fake images from publicly available pictures on social media. He’s concerned that strangers might use her pictures to create fake images with AI. He wants to protect Judy from this kind of problem. So, Chris wants to tell Judy that she should block strangers’ access to her pictures on social media. In this situation, what would Chris most likely say to Judy?

script.16:
[16～17] 다음을 듣고, 물음에 답하시오.
M: Welcome back to the Music and Life course. Songs are known to have several functions. Today, we’re learning about how songs are used at a variety of places to create group unity. First, people sing songs together in sports stadiums.
Most sports teams have unique fight songs that their fans sing to express connection to the team, which works as a kind of musical uniform that unites fans. Second, the use of songs promotes group identity at schools. Students sing their school song together during important events, which helps share common values and develops a sense of unity. Next, soldiers sing songs at military bases.
While they march and train, they sing their military songs together. Through this process, they build group bonds and develop into one unified force. Finally, people are brought together by work songs on farms. When people sing songs together while working on farms, they feel connected to one another and gain a sense of unity. Now, let’s listen to some example songs.
